def exchange(lst1, lst2):
    """In this problem, you will implement a function that takes two lists of numbers,
    and determines whether it is possible to perform exchanges to make lst1 
    a list of only even numbers.
    Elements can be exchanged between lst1 and lst2 to achieve this goal.
    If it is possible to make all the elements of lst1 even through exchanges, 
    return "YES". Otherwise, return "NO".
    """

Clarification: Swapping any odd element of lst1 with any even element of lst2, one-for-one; the reference solution determines feasibility by checking whether lst2 has at least as many even numbers as lst1 has odd numbers (count(even in lst2) >= count(odd in lst1)).

Clarification: The function doesn't model list mutation directly; it counts odd elements in lst1 and even elements in lst2, and returns YES if lst2 has enough even elements to cover (replace) all of lst1's odd elements.

candidates.question: Are the lists allowed to be modified in any way other than swapping odd elements from lst1 with even elements from lst2?
candidates.answer: The check only ever cares about the COUNT of odd elements in lst1 vs even elements in lst2, not the actual swap mechanics; any scheme achieving 'lst1 all even' is implicitly assumed possible whenever even(lst2) >= odd(lst1).
